rationale: The abstract presents an end-to-end point-based SNN as the main action-recognition feature extractor; the event-to-neuronal-spike interface and full spiking boundary remain unresolved.

The abstract makes the SVT-to-ISTA correspondence central and places an SNN decoder downstream; PDF evidence is required to distinguish the algorithmic encoder from the whole task network and to map continuous exceptions.

The abstract identifies adaptive sampling as the main contribution and validates it with both spiking and non-spiking detectors; the sampler output and variant-specific boundaries require PDF inspection.
The abstract describes spiking-neuron event selection and aggregation before detection; neuron equations, MTF boundary and the scope of the fully-spiking claim require PDF evidence.
The abstract says SNN firing controls event-slice boundaries and an ANN supplies downstream feedback; the exact trigger, input aggregation and train-versus-inference coupling remain unresolved.

The abstract couples event streams to a LIF-inspired feature extractor and an SSM but does not establish whether discrete neuronal spikes are transmitted or whether the layer is an explicit representation interface rather than a hidden feature module.

PDF inspection confirmed PLIF spike/reset dynamics, exposed a separate Poisson rate-code axis, and limited the fully-spiking claim to the learned task network rather than point preprocessing or the sensor-to-result pipeline.
The PDF substantiated the ISTA-variable mapping and a separate SNN decoder, while showing that the reconstructed image is a terminal membrane readout and energy is analytically estimated.
The PDF showed a continuous early aggregate, spike-delimited local samples, potential embeddings and four materially different detector boundaries, requiring configuration-level rows.

The paper confirms a genuine gated recurrent spiking selector, but the MTF soft mask and ANN compatibility paths change the boundary; four rows preserve these differences without multiplying paper counts.

The SNN truly triggers slice boundaries, but it receives voxel event cells rather than raw address events and remains a small front-end to an ANN task model; ANN neighborhood feedback is training-only.

The PDF confirms threshold/reset LIF output events and native timestamp updates, while the continuous EA-HiPPO/FFT state path and linear readout make the overall model hybrid; the interface-versus-embedded boundary remains queued for Astra.
The abstract presents HsVT as the event-detection task network but does not identify which spatial, temporal, attention and head operators are genuinely spiking.
The abstract explicitly places sparse SNN blocks and a bridge inside an ANN backbone; PDF evidence is needed to determine the SNN block boundary and whether hardware results cover the full detector.

The abstract assigns motion-feature extraction to an SNN branch and color processing to an ANN, suggesting an embedded SNN module whose neuron configuration and fusion boundary require PDF inspection.

The abstract claims a fully spiking frame-event tracking network with convolutional and Transformer components; modality encoders, attention, fusion, head and readout must be checked before assigning an extent.

The complete abstract explicitly limits the method to RGB tracking, making it an SNN task-network foundation/identity contrast rather than an event-camera intersection paper unless the PDF contradicts that input scope.

The abstract makes the event-tracking SNN the principal inference path and distinguishes integer-valued training activations from spike inference; PDF inspection must verify the mapping and full task boundary.
The abstract explicitly maps WTA circuits and STDP to EM E- and M-steps, making algorithmic_engine the initial hypothesis while continuous warping/readout boundaries remain unresolved.
The contribution is SNN-specific relevance propagation and event augmentation rather than a new inference topology, so it is initially placed cross-cutting with no new primary inference role.
The contribution attacks raw event data under sparsity constraints and evaluates existing SNN victims; it is an event-specific robustness/analysis paper, not a new inference-role representative.

Fixed-duration event sequences enter a four-stage hybrid detector whose main task path interleaves MaxViT, SpikingMLP, LSTM and an STFE module. This is a task_network rather than an embedded_module because the SNN components recur throughout the proposed backbone, although the backbone is not fully spiking.

A four-layer PLIF SNN extracts fast low-level features and hands them through ASAB to a larger continuous ANN detector. The SNN is therefore an embedded_module rather than the task_network, while the proposed system-level contribution is the complete hybrid backbone.

The SNN is the event-specific motion-feature branch inside a dual-drive ANN/SNN deblurring model. It is embedded_module rather than task_network because continuous image encoding, cross-modal fusion and the MIMO reconstruction decoder remain essential task components.

Both modality-specific feature extraction, spike self-attention fusion and decoupled tracking heads are designed in the spiking paradigm. The SNN therefore supplies the principal task network; the final continuous prediction convolutions prevent a stronger sensor-to-result purity claim.

RGB template/search images drive an NI-LIF spiking Siamese tracker with a memory-retrieval module and spike-driven head. It is a genuine SNN task_network but not an event-camera intersection paper; its value is as a controlled architecture comparator to the separate event-based paper with the same short name.

I-LIF convolutional blocks, DI-LIF spiking transformers and an I-LIF tracking head constitute the event tracker’s principal task path. The role is task_network; event voxelization is fixed preprocessing rather than a learned event_interface.

Warped address events charge stochastic IF neurons in a WTA circuit, whose firing implements EM responsibilities while STDP updates motion parameters. This is algorithmic_engine rather than task_network because spike variables are explicitly identified with E/M-step quantities and the central contribution is that algorithmic equivalence.

EventRPG changes training-time relevance propagation and augmentation around existing SNN classifiers; it does not add a new inference SNN topology. Primary role is therefore not_applicable rather than task_network, and the paper belongs on the cross-cutting training/analysis axis.

The proposed component is a white-box optimizer that perturbs raw event coordinates/polarities before an existing SNN classifier. It creates no new inference SNN function, so primary role is not_applicable and the paper belongs to cross-cutting robustness rather than task_network.
The abstract proposes a generally applicable binary-output neuron and temporal-gradient path; any event-camera relevance appears to be evaluation rather than an event-specific interface.
The contribution is a generic ANN-to-SNN conversion/calibration route, not a new event-specific inference role; task models and conversion boundaries require PDF confirmation.
STEP evaluates existing Spiking Transformers across static, event and sequential datasets; it is initially treated as an evaluation authority rather than core role evidence.
The abstract describes asynchronous sparse graph computation and hardware projections but no neuronal state, firing or reset; PDF must distinguish event-driven GNN from SNN.
PEPNet is initially an event-camera point-network comparator: raw event point clouds and an A-Bi-LSTM are explicit, while no SNN mechanism is claimed.
REDIR explicitly inserts an attention-enhanced SNN block into a pure-event reconstruction system; embedded_module is the initial hypothesis pending registration/decoder boundary checks.
Despite the event-based-vision title, the abstract presents ABN as a generic homeostatic neuron; PDF must establish whether event input changes the method or only benchmarks it.
FARSE-CNN is asynchronous, recurrent and sparse, but the abstract does not claim spiking neurons; it is treated as an event-only comparator until the recurrence equations are checked.

CLIF replaces standard neurons throughout directly trained VGG/ResNet SNN classifiers, so the evaluated SNN is a task_network; event-camera datasets only benchmark a generic neuron contribution and do not make it an event-specific interface or module.

The contribution is a post-training ANN-to-SNN conversion and calibration procedure spanning several pre-existing task architectures. Conversion is a training route, not a distinct inference role, so primary role is not_applicable.

STEP standardizes and analyzes existing Spiking Transformer implementations rather than adding an inference SNN component. Its taxonomy role is therefore not_applicable and its value lies in evaluation authority.

Directed event graphs feed continuous GNN and recurrent/convolutional periodic branches; no neuron firing or reset participates in computation. It has no SNN inference role and is retained only as an asynchronous event-method comparator.

Normalized x-y-time event points are processed by a hierarchical point network, attentive bidirectional LSTM and continuous pose regressor. The method is non-spiking, so it has no SNN functional role.

A three-layer TSA-LIF block filters persistent target events and occlusion noise inside a larger UNet/STN registration and CNN reconstruction system. It is an embedded_module rather than task_network because continuous registration, mask fusion and decoding remain indispensable.

Each camera event is injected as a spike into an SNN whose LIF/SRM neurons use ABN dynamic thresholds for classification and event-wise segmentation. The SNN is the principal task path, so this is task_network rather than a separate event interface.

Raw events update sparse convolutional LSTM cells and propagate continuous feature events through FARSE-CNN. Despite being asynchronous and stateful, it has no neuronal threshold, firing or reset, so no SNN role applies.

PPLN uses membrane terminology and neuromorphic motivation, but the abstract does not establish thresholded neuronal firing; PDF must resolve whether its piecewise temporal functions are actually spiking.
DailyDVS-200 is a physical event-camera action dataset and benchmark contribution; PDF is needed only for acquisition and split authority, not to infer an SNN role from neuromorphic wording.

The complete abstract explicitly identifies an intensity-integrating spike camera rather than a contrast-event camera and does not claim SNN computation; this is a terminology negative eligible for abstract-only closure.
SpikeGCL is an SNN method for ordinary graph benchmarks, not event-camera graph data; without an indispensable bridge to the survey, the abstract is sufficient for a scope/use negative.
MOTOR uses event to mean clinical time-to-event records and describes a conventional self-supervised foundation model; both target axes are absent, so no PDF is needed.

The attack uses DVS benchmarks and retimes existing input spikes under discrete grid constraints; PDF must establish whether the threat surface is physical event time, binned event input, neuronal spike time, or a generic SNN benchmark.

The abstract establishes event-only on-device self-supervised depth but no neuron firing; PDF must distinguish continuous contrast-maximization learning and measured hardware evidence from SNN/local-plasticity claims.

PPLN is a real-valued input-conditioned piecewise temporal function used inside conventional convolutional task networks. The paper explicitly distinguishes it from binary-spike communication and does not impose firing threshold, reset or refractory dynamics, so membrane terminology does not create an SNN role.

DailyDVS-200 contributes physical event-camera data, protocols and attribute-stratified evaluation. It includes spike-based baselines among twelve algorithms but proposes no SNN inference component, so it is benchmark authority rather than an SNN role exemplar.

The official abstract concerns intensity-integrating spike-camera streams and Gaussian-splatting reconstruction, not contrast-event-camera input or an asserted SNN computation; no survey inference role applies.

SpikeGCL applies spiking networks to ordinary graph contrastive learning. The abstract provides no event-camera signal or indispensable mechanism bridge to the target intersection, so inference-role fields are intentionally not extracted for this excluded record.

MOTOR uses event in the clinical time-to-event sense and models structured medical records with a conventional foundation model. It contains neither target sensor events nor spiking neural computation.

The contribution is an event-input retiming attack and robustness analysis over existing directly trained SNN victims, not a new inference module. It belongs to the core intersection as cross-cutting evidence with primary inference role not_applicable.

The system accumulates events into dense frames and trains a conventional convolutional/ConvGRU depth-and-egomotion network by contrast maximization. It demonstrates on-device online event learning without neuronal firing, so it is a full-system comparator rather than an SNN role.
Real-valued PPLN functions replace convolution/MLP operators and explicitly differ from binary-spike SNN communication.
WTA firing implements responsibilities/E-step and STDP updates motion parameters/M-step, while warping, TPE/SVD initialization and numerical IWE operations remain continuous.
Gated recurrent spiking neurons select events and emit an aggregated representation for either a fully spiking detector or conventional ANN detector variants.
The contribution is a timing-only attack on event-grid inputs to existing SNN victims, not a new inference topology.
The LIF front-end emits a new explicit event train, then pooling hands it to a continuous EA-HiPPO principal model; the codebook's handoff contract favors event_interface over embedded_module.
Direct event input drives a spiking MLP whose adaptive LIF/SRM neurons perform the classification and event-wise segmentation task path.
I-LIF convolution and tracking head plus DI-LIF transformer carry the principal tracking path, but final learned numerical prediction convolutions prevent a fully-spiking-task-network label.
ARSNN firing defines local sample boundaries and aggregated embeddings handed to several SNN/ANN detector configurations, so role is interface and extent must remain a configuration signature.
SLTRP/SLRP and relevance-guided event augmentation depend jointly on SNN temporal states and event input, but introduce no new inference SNN role.
MaxViT attention, SpikingMLP, LSTM and STFE jointly form the principal detector, making it a hybrid task network rather than a detachable local SNN module.
